newsitem.title: UK: Copper spread in contango, first time since Jan 95.
newsitem.headline: Copper spread in contango, first time since Jan 95.

text.p: Cash copper traded at a discount to three month delivery prices, or in a "contango", for the first time since January 1995, when the benchmark London Metal Exchange spread eased to $2 contango in early Tuesday business.
This ends a prolonged period of cash premiums over forward values, or "backwardations". The spread ended on Monday at $8/9 backwardation.
Copper spread in contango, first time since Jan 95
Traders said the disappearance of the cash metal premium reflects the recent trend of easing availability of metal for nearby delivery, with world demand weak despite falling stocks.
Tuesday's small contango ends an extended period of backwardations, which in recent months peaked at $330 a tonne.

Traders said cash premiums often reflected a squeeze on nearby copper availability engineered by Sumitomo Corp's former star trader Yasuo Hamanaka, dubbed the world's biggest copper trader until his unauthorised losses were revealed in mid-June.

Traders said there were still pockets of supply tightness centred around certain delivery dates in November and December, but they were not causing concern. "No-one really wants metal at the moment," a trader said.
